en: The Therāpadāna, Subhūti Chapter: 5.
The Apadāna of the Elder Anna-saṃsāvaka
“The perfectly enlightened one, golden-hued,
resembling a priceless ornament of gold, was walking through the marketplace.”
To Siddhattha, the lamp of the world, immeasurable and incomparable, who possesses the thirty-two excellent marks.
I attained supreme joy upon seeing the Tamer,
the Radiant One; having bowed down to the Perfectly Enlightened One, I—
I fed that great sage;
the Greatly Compassionate One in the world then expressed his appreciation for me.
Having inspired confidence in the mind toward that Buddha, the Great Compassionate One, the provider of supreme consolation,
I rejoiced in heaven for an eon.
Ninety-four eons ago,
the gift that I gave at that time—
I do not know a state of woe;
this is the fruit of giving alms-food.
The four analytical knowledges—
And these eight liberations have been realized; the six direct knowledges have been attained;
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.”
Thus indeed the venerable elder Anna-saṃsāvaka spoke these verses.
This is the fifth legend of the elder Anna-saṃsāvaka.
